questions.answer: Writing 5.0000 kg claims more precision than a rough benchmark comparison supports. A useful physical check is that one student can lift the loaded bag but can still feel that it has a mass of several kilograms.
accepted_alternatives: Any valid explanation of false precision plus a relevant benchmark, lifting or scale-bracketing check
questions.unit_policy: No new numerical estimate is required. A check may refer to kilograms when describing the expected scale.
questions.tolerance: Accept any physically sensible check that tests whether a mass of about 5 kg is plausible for a loaded school bag.

marking_points.text: Explains that 5.0000 kg claims more precision than the rough estimating evidence supports
States a relevant physical benchmark or plausibility check for the mass of a loaded school bag

questions.unit_policy: No written unit is required because the learner selects one complete option.

marking_points.text: Selects electric current with ampere as the correct SI base quantity-unit pair

option_feedback.A: Correct. Electric current is an SI base quantity and the ampere is its SI base unit.
option_feedback.B: Temperature is a base quantity, but its SI base unit is the kelvin, not degree Celsius.
option_feedback.C: Mass is a base quantity, but its SI base unit is the kilogram, not the gram.
option_feedback.D: Length is a base quantity, but its SI base unit is the metre. A kilometre is a prefixed multiple of the metre.

questions.unit_policy: No unit is required because the learner selects a prefix symbol.

marking_points.text: Selects M as the prefix symbol for the multiplier 10^6

option_feedback.A: Lower-case m is milli and represents 10^-3.
option_feedback.B: The symbol μ is micro and represents 10^-6.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Capital M is mega and represents 10^6.
option_feedback.D: Capital G is giga and represents 10^9.

questions.unit_policy: No written unit is required because the learner selects one complete option.

marking_points.text: Selects 4.2 μm as equal to 0.0000042 m

option_feedback.A: Nano represents 10^-9, so 4.2 nm is 4.2 x 10^-9 m and is too small.
option_feedback.C: Milli represents 10^-3, so 4.2 mm is 0.0042 m and is too large.
option_feedback.D: Kilo represents 10^3, so 4.2 km is 4200 m and is far too large.

questions.answer: mass: kilogram (kg); length: metre (m); time: second (s); electric current: ampere (A); temperature: kelvin (K).
accepted_alternatives: current for electric current when the ampere and A are both correct
questions.unit_policy: Both the unit name and correctly cased symbol are required for each pair.
questions.tolerance: Spelling variants may be accepted, but symbol case must be correct.

questions.answer: Micro means 10^-6, so 3.2 μs = 3.2 x 10^-6 s. Milli means 10^-3, so 4.5 ms = 4.5 x 10^-3 s. Also 0.0060 s = 6.0 x 10^-3 s. The order from shortest to longest is 3.2 μs, 4.5 ms, 0.0060 s.
questions.unit_policy: Seconds must be attached to both converted values. The final ordering may use the original labelled forms.
questions.tolerance: Exact conversions are required. Equivalent scientific or decimal notation is accepted.

marking_points.text: Uses the micro multiplier 10^-6 for 3.2 μs
Converts 3.2 μs to 3.2 x 10^-6 s
Uses the milli multiplier 10^-3 for 4.5 ms
Converts 4.5 ms to 4.5 x 10^-3 s
Orders the durations as 3.2 μs, 4.5 ms, 0.0060 s from shortest to longest

questions.answer: 2.05 km = 2050 m; 205 cm = 2.05 m; 2.05 mm = 0.00205 m. A classroom door is about two metres high, so 205 cm, or 2.05 m, is the plausible label. The SI base quantity is length and its SI base-unit symbol is m.
accepted_alternatives: 2.050 x 10^3 m, 2.05 m and 2.05 x 10^-3 m with an equivalent physical justification
questions.unit_policy: Metres must be attached to all three converted values. The base-unit symbol must be lower-case m.
questions.tolerance: Exact conversions are required. The plausibility justification must identify a door-height scale near 2 m.

Converts 2.05 mm to 0.00205 m
Identifies 205 cm or 2.05 m as the plausible door height and supports it with a reasonable scale comparison
Identifies length as the SI base quantity being measured
